title: T-Mobile’s secret $25/month plan is tempting, but here’s why I won’t sign up
title_bn: টি-মোবাইলের গোপন ২৫ ডলার প্লেনটা বেশ প্রলুব্ধকর, কিন্তু আমি কেন সাইন আপ করবো না সেটা এখানে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: You can do a lot better than T-Mobile's new budget plan.
paragraph1: Joe Maring / Android AuthorityAdd Android Authority on Google: Recently, we learned about a secret T-Mobile plan that costs just $25 per month, significantly undercutting every major US carrier. Before you rush out and sign up, however, you’ll want to make sure you understand exactly what you’re getting.On paper, the offer sounds compelling and, in a vacuum, it really is. That said, there are a few caveats you should consider before making up your mind.Is T-Mobile's new Super Essentials Saver worth signing up for?1 votesWhat is T-Mobile’s Super Essentials Saver plan?The Super Essentials Saver plan appears to offer all the features you’d get from T-Mobile’s standard Essentials plan. You get unlimited 5G data, the same 50GB of premium high-speed access, and unlimited 3G mobile hotspot usage running at 3G speeds. It even retains coverage in Mexico and Canada, alongside unlimited texting from the US to over 215 countries.So, what’s the catch? There are a few minor “gotchas.” First, the $25 price tag doesn’t include taxes and fees, which typically add another $5 to $8 per line. You are also capped at a maximum of two lines, and there is no multi-line discount.
paragraph2: Super Essentials Saver is a great deal over standard Essentials or Essentials Saver. But is it really the best option?The biggest restriction, however, is that you must be a new customer and physically visit a Walmart store to sign up, as this offer is exclusive to the big-box retailer.It’s currently unclear how long this promotion will last or whether there are any hidden downsides not immediately apparent on paper. While I haven’t found any major drawbacks compared to the standard $50 Essentials plan, be aware that you won’t see many (if any) promotional phone deals.This lack of hardware promos has largely held true for the standard Essentials tier for a while, though occasional special deals have been available in the past. It’s safe to assume this Super Saver plan will be completely devoid of promotional phone upgrades, but only time will tell.Why I’d pick Verizon Simplicity over T-Mobile’s new planJoe Maring / Android AuthorityIn many ways, Verizon Simplicity and T-Mobile Super Essentials Saver are very similar. Both plans offer an entry-level experience built around unlimited data and international roaming in Canada and Mexico.Technically, Verizon Simplicity costs $15 more per month than T-Mobile’s new Walmart plan. However, customers switching from another carrier can get it for just $30 a month. For those keeping score, that’s only $5 more than T-Mobile’s offering.While T-Mobile’s Walmart exclusive looks like a better deal at a glance, Verizon’s Simplicity plan remains the more tempting offer.
paragraph3: First, consider the line limits: while T-Mobile caps you at two lines, Verizon Simplicity allows up to 12 lines at the $30 price point. For large families, Verizon presents a much better long-term value.Verizon gives you better hotspot access and a few other extras that make it stand out — like support for up to 12 lines. Verizon doesn’t offer unlimited hotspot access, but it does include 10GB of high-speed hotspot data (even if it’s lower-priority). Verizon’s hotspot might be limited, but it will be noticeably faster than T-Mobile’s claimed 3G speeds. Most users report a cap of around 600Kbps. I’d much rather have functional, usable hotspot speeds limited to 10GB than unlimited, garbage-quality speeds any day of the week.Edgar Cervantes / Android AuthorityIf you travel frequently or live in a rural area as I do, you’ll likely find that Verizon offers the superior network, though this naturally varies depending on exactly where you live. T-Mobile’s rural coverage has improved significantly, and its main markets are among the fastest in the US, but Verizon remains more consistent nationwide.As expected with budget plans, Verizon’s base Simplicity tier doesn’t support phone promotions, meaning you’ll need to buy your phone outright or sign up for a standard payment plan. However, the Simplicity Plus and Pro add-ons offer greater upgrade flexibility for $35 and $50 per month, respectively.With these add-ons, you receive a monthly credit that covers a phone payment plan indefinitely, along with the option to upgrade annually. The cheaper Plus add-on covers phones up to $850, while the Pro tier raises that credit limit to devices valued up to $1,300.
paragraph4: While I don’t think these add-ons are worth it for most people, they highlight another area where Verizon’s plan is far more flexible than T-Mobile’s new offering.Prepaid isn’t any cheaper, but it still might be betterJoe Maring / Android AuthorityFor the first time in recent memory, two of the three largest US carriers are offering postpaid plans in the same price range as some of the cheapest unlimited prepaid plans. Because many consumers still view prepaid as a lesser experience, these budget tiers make Verizon and T-Mobile look incredibly appealing. Just be aware that paying the same price doesn’t guarantee the same experience.Postpaid plans typically hold advantages over prepaid carriers, such as more features, better financing options, and superior device insurance. The catch here is that T-Mobile and Verizon have dramatically watered down the features and phone promotions on these budget plans. You are mostly paying for the brand name, as the standard postpaid perks simply don’t apply or are heavily restricted.Visible and other prepaid carriers might not cost any less, but many of these plans offer extras that the cheaper Verizon and T-Mobile plans are lacking. While Verizon and T-Mobile’s high-end plans absolutely outcompete a prepaid option like Visible Plus in terms of features, the opposite is true at this budget tier. With Visible Plus, you currently pay $29 per month, including taxes and fees.For that price, you get true HD video streaming, rather than the 720p cap typical of budget postpaid offerings. You also get unlimited premium data and unlimited hotspot access capped at a very usable 10Mbps. Furthermore, the international data options are vastly superior.
paragraph5: Not only do you get unlimited talk, text, and data in Mexico and Canada, but you also receive one Global Pass day per month (which can accrue up to 12 days).Visible is arguably one of the best overall values right now in both the prepaid and postpaid markets, but you’ll find a similarly competitive experience with prepaid carriers like US Mobile or Mint Mobile.Which is the right pick for you?Edgar Cervantes / Android AuthorityPersonally, I’d gladly take Verizon or Visible over T-Mobile’s new plan. The “Un-carrier” has always been less impressive in my rural Midwestern neck of the woods, and the potential $5 in monthly savings isn’t worth giving up Verizon’s network reliability.If your situation sounds similar, I highly recommend looking closer at prepaid options. The same advice applies if you want to spend under $40 per month but still want premium features like better international coverage, high-priority data, and usable hotspot speeds. The major carriers offer all of these perks, but you’ll pay close to triple the price to get them on a standard postpaid plan.That said, some users are absolutely set on sticking to a major brand for perceived advantages, such as marginally better customer support, simple installment plans, or specific add-ons and insurance. In those cases, Verizon Simplicity is the clear winner.Ultimately, unless you absolutely prefer T-Mobile’s network in your specific region, you are likely better off looking elsewhere.FollowThank you for being part of our community. title: We tested DLSS 5 in NBA 2K27 with every RTX 50-series GPU — first official release comes with a big performance hit, but almost every Blackwell card can run it at 1080p
title_bn: আমরা এনবিএ ২কে২৭-এ DLSS ৫-কে প্রতিটি RTX ৫০-সিরিজের জিপিইউ-র সাথে পরীক্ষা করেছি  প্রথম আনুষ্ঠানিক রিলিজটি বড় পারফরম্যান্স হিটের সাথে আসে কিন্তু প্রায় প্রতিটি ব্ল্যাকওয়েল কার্ড এটি 1080p-এ চালাতে পারে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: We tested Nvidia's DLSS 5 in NBA 2K27 across every RTX 50-series graphics card at 1080p, 1440p, and 4K to see just how much performance it costs to explore the frontiers of neural rendering.
paragraph1: (Image credit: 2K) Nvidia's DLSS 5 has arrived in NBA 2K27, and we've been up since midnight testing it across every RTX 50-series graphics card to see what the first official implementation of this tech can do and how it compares to the community-implemented mods that have been circulating over the past couple weeks.Before we discuss the performance cost of DLSS 5, many will ask whether this tech is even worth getting excited about, given the intense controversy that it's sparked ever since Nvidia revealed it earlier this year.In short: yes, absolutely.This first-party implementation of DLSS 5, tuned under the full control of 2K Games' art directors and artists, looks incredible, full stop. If you see it running, you will want to leave it on. It doesn't look like "slop" or a cheap filter. It just looks correct, or at least more correct. Image 1 of 2 (Image credit: 2K) For just a couple of examples, without DLSS 5, even at ultra settings and with RT, the game has a slightly "plastic" or "flat" look. Faces can have a waxy uniformity that immediately indicates that you're looking at a video game, not a live broadcast. Hair looks totally and unnaturally flat. The whites of eyes can be unnaturally bright, giving a sort of googly-eye or doll-like effect that immediately broke my sense of immersion. I didn't think any of this would be a big deal for a sports game, but it all stands out.
paragraph2: Image 1 of 2 (Image credit: 2K) DLSS 5 breathes incredible life into NBA 2K27. Skin looks like real flesh and blood. Eyes are rendered with the proper tones, depth, and sparkle. Hair looks a billion times more realistic. Every human on screen just looks more alive. You won't entirely forget that you're looking at a game, but it becomes much easier to suspend disbelief and get lost in the action.My experience slapping DLSS 5 mods into games has produced promising but sometimes mixed results. If the polished experience that NBA 2K25 delivers is any indication, I can't wait for more studios to get their hands on it and integrate it into their games under the care of the same artists that created them.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Our testing methodsWe did our best to deliver clean test numbers in the short time we've had with NBA 2K27. Performance in this can be tricky to measure. Benchmarking in the hub worlds or cutscenes will deliver lower performance than on the court, and even then, in-game events like fouls and time-outs will also result in skewed numbers if you're not careful.
paragraph3: We picked a repeatable match-up from the game's career mode and sampled 60 seconds of continuous gameplay with DLSS 5 on and off, making sure to restart if we ran into any of the scripted events above.We used NBA 2K27's maximum graphics settings as our baseline, including RT. We tested at native resolutions without upscaling, and we didn't test with Multi Frame Generation enabled. We view MFG as a cherry on top of an already solid baseline experience, not a baseline in itself.Our test system is built with the following components: Swipe to scroll horizontally Tom's Hardware 2026 GPU Test System CPU AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D CPU Cooler Thermalright Phantom Spirit 120SE Memory 32GB (2x16GB) G.Skill Trident Z5 Neo DDR5-6000 CL30 Motherboard Asus TUF Gaming X670E-Plus Wifi Storage Inland Performance Plus 4TB PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD Power supply MSI MPG Ai1600TS 1600W Operating system Windows 11 Pro Graphics driver version GeForce Game Ready 616.64 All of our performance results are captured using Nvidia's FrameView 2.0 utility. We measure graphics card power consumption directly with Nvidia's PCAT hardware power logging tool.If you have any questions about our testing methods, let us know in the comments and we'll do our best to answer them. On to the numbers.
paragraph4: NBA 2K27 1080p performance (Image credit: Future)At 1080p, everything from the RTX 5070 on up is CPU-bound without DLSS 5 enabled, even with maxed-out settings and RT on. Turn on DLSS 5, though, and the differences in Tensor Core compute across the cards quickly becomes obvious. But even the RTX 5060 can manage nearly 60 FPS on average with DLSS 5 enabled at 1080p, so almost anybody with a Blackwell card can at least try out the feature.Given these results, you might think to enable DLSS Super Resolution (aka upscaling). But because the amount of time needed to run the DLSS 5 model has a fixed cost per output frame that scales with your target resolution and largely dominates the total frame time, especially on lower-end hardware, you may find that enabling DLSS SR doesn't have as much of an effect on performance as we've come to expect. The game still has to wait for that final generative step to occur, even if DLSS SR cuts down some of the total frame time.As noted, we didn't use MFG for these tests, simply because there's no need for us to make the numbers on these charts artifically large. If you do want to enable it, the multiplier you want will be determined by your monitor's refresh rate and your own personal tastes. (Image credit: Future)We did chart PC latency as estimated by FrameView, so you can get a sense of whether there's enough of a latency budget to enable MFG at all. At 1080p, every card is a solid candidate for enabling MFG without adding unreasonable amounts of input latency, although the RTX 5050 is in a borderline position. And all three of the 8GB cards might have trouble fitting the MFG model into their VRAM with these maxed-out settings and DLSS 5 enabled, so you might need to turn off RT at a minimum to use MFG on these lower-end GPUs. (Image credit: Future)As we already saw in early testing of the leaked DLSS 5 builds circulating in the community, enabling the model has a large impact on power consumption, likely due to the intense Tensor Core load required to run the DLSS 5 model.
paragraph5: NBA 2K27 1440p performance (Image credit: Future)Moving up to 1440p separates our cards some more. The RTX 5080 and RTX 5090 are still CPU-limited without DLSS 5. The RTX 5060 Ti 8GB, RTX 5060, and RTX 5050 all get a "Low VRAM" warning with these settings, so if you're trying to push this higher resolution with those cards, you might want to start tuning your DLSS upscaling settings to relieve VRAM pressure, even if it doesn't result in additional performance with DLSS 5. (Image credit: Future)But you really want an RTX 5060 Ti at a minimum here to get acceptable input latency with DLSS 5 enabled, and the RTX 5070 is the true baseline for a good experience. At the higher end, the RTX 5070 Ti and RTX 5080 both provide fluid frame rates even without MFG, and you have the latency budget to enable framegen without worry on anything from the RTX 5070 on up. (Image credit: Future)DLSS 5's power consumption on all these cards (except the chugging RTX 5050) rises as expected with the higher-resolution output frame we're asking it to generate. Everything from the RTX 5060 up to the RTX 5070 Ti ends up running at its power limit, while the RTX 5080 and RTX 5090 still have room to stretch out. The unconstrained MSI RTX 5090 Lighting Z sucks down a ton of power to deliver its scorching performance.NBA 2K27 4K performance (Image credit: Future)Running NBA 2K27 at 4K with DLSS 5 is extremely demanding, since the model has to generate an output frame with more than twice as many pixels than at 1440p. Even the RTX 5070 Ti is straining here, as its input latency with DLSS 5 is potentially too high to enable MFG while still delivering a responsive gameplay experience. (Image credit: Future)You can see why Nvidia only recommends the RTX 5080 and RTX 5090 for a 4K DLSS 5 experience in this title, as they're the only two cards that deliver high enough baseline performance with low enough input latencies to make MFG practical.

But because the amount of time needed to run the DLSS 5 model has a fixed cost per output frame that scales with your target resolution and largely dominates the total frame time, especially on lower-end hardware, you may find that enabling DLSS SR doesn't have as much of an effect on performance as we've come to expect. The game still has to wait for that final generative step to occur, even if DLSS SR cuts down some of the total frame time.As noted, we didn't use MFG for these tests, simply because there's no need for us to make the numbers on these charts artifically large. If you do want to enable it, the multiplier you want will be determined by your monitor's refresh rate and your own personal tastes. (Image credit: Future)We did chart PC latency as estimated by FrameView, so you can get a sense of whether there's enough of a latency budget to enable MFG at all. At 1080p, every card is a solid candidate for enabling MFG without adding unreasonable amounts of input latency, although the RTX 5050 is in a borderline position. And all three of the 8GB cards might have trouble fitting the MFG model into their VRAM with these maxed-out settings and DLSS 5 enabled, so you might need to turn off RT at a minimum to use MFG on these lower-end GPUs. (Image credit: Future)As we already saw in early testing of the leaked DLSS 5 builds circulating in the community, enabling the model has a large impact on power consumption, likely due to the intense Tensor Core load required to run the DLSS 5 model.
bangla_paragraph5: NBA 2K27 1440p performance (Image credit: Future)Moving up to 1440p separates our cards some more. The RTX 5080 and RTX 5090 are still CPU-limited without DLSS 5. The RTX 5060 Ti 8GB, RTX 5060, and RTX 5050 all get a "Low VRAM" warning with these settings, so if you're trying to push this higher resolution with those cards, you might want to start tuning your DLSS upscaling settings to relieve VRAM pressure, even if it doesn't result in additional performance with DLSS 5. (Image credit: Future)But you really want an RTX 5060 Ti at a minimum here to get acceptable input latency with DLSS 5 enabled, and the RTX 5070 is the true baseline for a good experience. At the higher end, the RTX 5070 Ti and RTX 5080 both provide fluid frame rates even without MFG, and you have the latency budget to enable framegen without worry on anything from the RTX 5070 on up. (Image credit: Future)DLSS 5's power consumption on all these cards (except the chugging RTX 5050) rises as expected with the higher-resolution output frame we're asking it to generate. Everything from the RTX 5060 up to the RTX 5070 Ti ends up running at its power limit, while the RTX 5080 and RTX 5090 still have room to stretch out. The unconstrained MSI RTX 5090 Lighting Z sucks down a ton of power to deliver its scorching performance.NBA 2K27 4K performance (Image credit: Future)Running NBA 2K27 at 4K with DLSS 5 is extremely demanding, since the model has to generate an output frame with more than twice as many pixels than at 1440p. Even the RTX 5070 Ti is straining here, as its input latency with DLSS 5 is potentially too high to enable MFG while still delivering a responsive gameplay experience. (Image credit: Future)You can see why Nvidia only recommends the RTX 5080 and RTX 5090 for a 4K DLSS 5 experience in this title, as they're the only two cards that deliver high enough baseline performance with low enough input latencies to make MFG practical.

title: Robotaxis enter their villain era
title_bn: রোবোট্যাক্সি তাদের দুষ্টু যুগে প্রবেশ করে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: It's Bullitt meets Christine meets Waymo. A new short film imagines a San Francisco car chase where the other driver isn't human - and the car may be trying to kill you. That a robotaxi can now be cast as the villain with almost no explanation says s
paragraph1: It’s Bullitt meets Christine meets Waymo.A new short film imagines a San Francisco car chase where the other driver isn’t human — and the car may be trying to kill you. That a robotaxi can now be cast as the villain with almost no explanation says something about the present moment. Autonomous cars have gone from sci-fi curiosities to fixtures in some American cities, where they’ve become stand-ins for anxieties about AI job displacement, Big Tech surveillance, and machines making decisions once left to humans.Road Rage, the planned short film awaiting $40,000 on Kickstarter to fund production, leans into all of it. The film pits Joa, a ridehail driver in a manual-transmission car, against Roboride, an autonomous vehicle that takes a minor road-rage incident very personally, according to a synopsis by its director, Romain Thomassin. Roboride lightly clips Joa’s mirror. Joa gives it the finger. The car decides to kill him.“It’s analog versus artificial,” Thomassin told The Verge.The AI bad guy will be played by an old Prius transformed with cold LED lights across the front — à la Tesla — fake cameras, a spinning lidar-like device on the roof, a black exterior, and a menacing, ever-blinking red dot. Thomassin calls the intended result a “nasty Waymo.”“I really wanted to play the nasty, gritty look of the ’70s car chase, but with today’s robotaxi in today’s San Francisco,” he said.
paragraph2: The chase itself will be a throwback: real cars, real actors, and real stunts.“I really wanted to play the nasty, gritty look of the ’70s car chase, but with today’s robotaxi in today’s San Francisco.”— Road Rage director Romain Thomassin“What makes Joa the good guy is not only his instinct but also his authenticity,” Thomassin said, noting a scene in which the character has an unexpected conversation with his passengers. “This type of human interaction doesn’t happen in a robotaxi.”Thomassin doesn’t actually think robotaxis are inherently evil. But as a movie villain, they come preloaded with tension. For one thing, they’re replacing the kind of worker his protagonist represents. Joa is a Mexican immigrant trying to make a living driving in an increasingly expensive San Francisco. Robotaxis are already competing with ridehail drivers, just as generative AI is competing with workers in Thomassin’s own industry.“Driving here is a metaphor for what’s happening in cinema, in filmmaking,” Thomassin said.1/4Guerilla posters for Road Rage. Image: Grace Vincent / Road RageThen there’s surveillance. Autonomous cars are covered in cameras and sensors, constantly observing the streets — and people — around them.
paragraph3: That, more than the prospect of being driven around without a human behind the wheel, is what actually unnerves Thomassin.In Road Rage, that anxiety is pushed toward dystopia. There’s a brief encounter involving immigration enforcement, and Thomassin imagines a feature-length version in which autonomous cars identify people, trap passengers inside, or deliver them directly to authorities. The progression, as he describes it, is observation, surveillance, then control.“The next step is that [autonomous vehicles] could become the police,” he said. And because robotaxis operate as connected fleets, the threat can scale beyond one vehicle. “Imagine an army rising up,” Thomassin said.Robotaxis also make unusually good revenge-movie villains because people already treat them like adversaries. Thomassin points to the indignities Waymos have endured on San Francisco streets: people immobilizing them with traffic cones, tagging and vandalizing them, and even setting them on fire.“They are being bullied,” he said. In Road Rage, that mistreatment becomes the motivation: “They want to take revenge.”Thomassin describes Roboride as absorbing the behavior it observes around it — including the behavior of human drivers. The car is simply learning road rage from humans.
paragraph4: “Humans are known to be the worst versions of themselves on the road,” he said.That makes Roboride a very 2026 update to the killer car idea in Stephen King’s Christine. There, the menace is supernatural. Here, it comes from something more contemporary: a machine that watches humans, learns from them, and inherits some of their worst traits along with the useful ones.On the other side of the chase is Joa and his stick shift — a deliberately analog counterpoint. To Thomassin, driving stick is a deeply human act: The driver remains in control of the vehicle, physically responding to the road. What separates Joa from Roboride, in Thomassin’s telling, is instinct — and even irrationality.During one confrontation, Joa takes his hands off the steering wheel while facing down the autonomous car. The move is so reckless that Roboride backs off. The human wins by becoming less predictable than the machine.“Respect your madness. Be a little mad and creative in your way of doing things, and you will be able to rise against the machines.”— Romain Thomassin“Respect your madness,” Thomassin said.
paragraph5: “Be a little mad and creative in your way of doing things, and you will be able to rise against the machines.”Despite its skepticism toward AI, Road Rage may use some of the technology itself. Thomassin says the filmmakers are considering AI-generated imagery to depict what Roboride sees, while shooting the human driver’s world with traditional cinematography. To him, that distinction matters. He sees AI as a creative tool when it serves the story, rather than simply a way to replace workers.For all the menace he sees in robotaxis, Thomassin isn’t afraid to ride in them. He signed up for Waymo as soon as he could and uses it when visiting friends and family for rides.“I don’t feel in danger,” he said.That may be what makes Roboride such an effective 2026 villain. The scary part isn’t necessarily that the machine will crash. The scary part is that the machine works.Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.

title: The Pixel 11 Pro should be a disappointment, but after 3 weeks with the phone I can’t put it down
title_bn: পিক্সেল ১১ প্রো হতাশাজনক হবে, কিন্তু ফোনটি ব্যবহারের ৩ সপ্তাহ পর আমি এটাকে আর নামাতে পারছি না।
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The Pixel 11 Pro isn't perfect, but I still love it.
paragraph1: The Pixel 11 Pro is an imperfect Android phone that's simultaneously a joy to use. It doesn't have a significantly more powerful Tensor chip, and new features like HiLight miss the mark. However, Google's proven formula of outstanding hardware, phenomenal cameras, and best-in-class Android software make it a phone I'll happily keep in my pocket for a while to come.Add Android Authority on Google: A lot has been said about the Pixel 11 Pro and 11 Pro XL since their unveiling on August 12 — much of it not very good. Pixel phones always come with an extra heaping of criticism, warranted or not, but there are real concerns about this year’s Pro phones. They have less RAM than last year’s models, HiLight has already proven disappointing, the Tensor G6 chip isn’t a particularly big performance upgrade, and the phones are more expensive than ever before.Considering all that, it would be safe to assume the Pixel 11 Pro ($1099 at Amazon) and Pixel 11 Pro XL ($1299 at Amazon) aren’t good phones. However, after spending about three weeks with both of them, I don’t think that could be further from the truth.In typical Google fashion, the Pixel 11 Pro and its XL sibling aren’t chasing the biggest specs, and some of the hallmark new features aren’t as amazing as Google wants you to think. But the day-to-day experience of using the phones still ignites that unmistakable Pixel magic, and imperfections aside, I plan to keep using the Pixel 11 Pro long after this review is finished.The 3 biggest disappointments — HiLight, Proactive Assistance, and chargingJoe Maring / Android AuthorityThere are some genuine complaints I have with the Pixel 11 Pro, despite how much I like it, so let’s get those out of the way first. There are three main things to talk about: HiLight, Proactive Assistance, and charging.
paragraph2: HiLight is the glowing light on the back of the 11 Pro and 11 Pro XL, and as you’ve probably heard by now, it barely does anything. You can assign colors to specific favorite contacts, and when you do, HiLight will light up when they call you. Additionally, if your Pixel is face down, HiLight pulses and swirls when you interact with Gemini. Neat!These are both fine features, but the problem is that they’re quite literally all HiLight does right now. Third-party apps have already unlocked more functionality, letting you use HiLight as a proper notification light for text messages and other apps, but the fact that this isn’t available out of the box is truly embarrassing. HiLight could be a great feature after ample updates, but right now, it’s not worth buying the Pixel 11 Pro for.Joe Maring / Android AuthorityProactive Assistance is equally disappointing. The pitch here is that your phone can proactively surface relevant info and actions based on what you’re doing. For example, if a friend texts you asking about an upcoming flight, Proactive Assistance can find your flight info and offer a shortcut to share it with them. Or, if you get a text asking if you’ve made a reservation at a restaurant for a certain time, you’ll get a shortcut in Google Messages to do it right there.That sounds cool on paper, but after almost a month with the Pixel 11 Pro, Proactive Assistance has proven genuinely useful not once.
paragraph3: There are a couple of reasons for this. First, you have to be very specific about how you use your phone to prompt Proactive Assistance. Many of its actions only work in Google Messages or the Phone app, and if your text threads don’t contain very specific dates and times, you’ll never see these pop-ups. Secondly, the handful of times Proactive Assistance has appeared on my Pixel 11 Pro, the suggestions haven’t been helpful. I know what restaurant my partner and I are going to — I don’t need or want a Gemini summary of it.Proactive Assistance has proven genuinely useful a grand total of zero times.The good news is that Proactive Assistance is easy enough to ignore if you don’t care about it, and like HiLight, it should get better over time. But three weeks in, it’s a dud.What won’t get better over time is the charging performance of the Pixel 11 Pro and 11 Pro XL. Both phones are rated for the same maximum wired charging speeds as their predecessors, at 30W and 45W, respectively. The big thing this year is a new “Extreme Charging Mode” that reduces background tasks to deliver faster charging when your phone is below 50%.Joe Maring / Android AuthorityIn reality, this doesn’t seem to make much of a difference at all.
paragraph4: The Pixel 11 Pro matches the Pixel 10 Pro almost exactly in our charging tests, with the 11 Pro taking 86 minutes to charge from 0-100% compared to 87 minutes for the 10 Pro. The Pixel 11 Pro XL’s faster 45W is a real benefit, taking just 64 minutes for a full charge, and topping up slightly faster than the 10 Pro XL. However, it’s still significantly slower than the Galaxy S26 Ultra’s 60W charging, which goes from dead to full in only 42 minutes.Joe Maring / Android AuthorityThese charge speeds are serviceable, and for overnight charging, you won’t have any issues. But in a world where even Samsung is finally getting on the fast-charging bandwagon, Google’s unwillingness to make any meaningful progress here is more grating than ever. Especially since the Pixel 11 Pro now starts at $1,099 and the 11 Pro XL will set you back at least $1,299, Google really should have done better.Tensor G6 isn’t a miracle chip, but it’s still very goodJoe Maring / Android AuthorityWith that out of the way, there is one more thing we should talk about before I really start gushing about the Pixel 11 Pro: the Tensor G6 chip.Right off the bat, I’ll say this. Day-to-day performance from the G6 on the Pixel 11 Pro is outstanding. The phone is extremely snappy, animations are as fluid as you could ask for, and my go-to mobile game (Call of Duty: Mobile) runs really well at High graphics and Max frame rate. For the way I use my phone, the Tensor G6 hasn’t given me any issues — and I’ve not noticed the Pixel 11 Pro heating up either. It’s been a really good experience.
paragraph5: That said, it has to be mentioned that the Tensor G6 still lacks significant raw horsepower versus the competition. Compared to the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 powering the Galaxy S26 and S26 Ultra, the Tensor G6 is worse in nearly every metric — delivering lower single-core and multi-core CPU speeds and significantly worse GPU performance (up to 58% slower in Wild Life Extreme 3DMark stress tests). The Tensor G6 delivers improved CPU performance compared to the Tensor G5 in the Pixel 10 Pro models, but I haven’t noticed any meaningful year-over-year difference.Joe Maring / Android AuthorityBenchmarks certainly aren’t everything, and as I said above, I’ve not had any real-world performance complaints with the Pixel 11 Pro after three weeks of regular use. I imagine most people who buy the 11 Pro or 11 Pro XL will find themselves in a similar boat. But if you want the absolute most performance from your next Android phone, you won’t find that here. That’s never been the point of Pixels, and I think that’s OK, but it’s still worth noting.One aspect of the Tensor G6 that’s unquestionably better is efficiency. The 4,850mAh battery in the Pixel 11 Pro and the 5,115mAh battery in Pixel 11 Pro XL are actually smaller than batteries in the Pixel 10 Pro and Pixel 10 Pro XL (4,870mAh and 5,200mAh, respectively), but this year’s phones still manage to last longer — and that’s all thanks to a more efficient chipset.Joe Maring / Android AuthorityI’ve primarily been using the small Pixel 11 Pro, and depending on what apps I’m using and how much of my time is spent on 5G, I’m seeing anywhere from four and a half to well over six hours of screen-on time, usually with around 20% battery still left in the tank. On the Pixel 10 Pro last year, I was topping out around five hours and hitting some days with just three hours of screen time.

Especially since the Pixel 11 Pro now starts at $1,099 and the 11 Pro XL will set you back at least $1,299, Google really should have done better.Tensor G6 isn’t a miracle chip, but it’s still very goodJoe Maring / Android AuthorityWith that out of the way, there is one more thing we should talk about before I really start gushing about the Pixel 11 Pro: the Tensor G6 chip.Right off the bat, I’ll say this. Day-to-day performance from the G6 on the Pixel 11 Pro is outstanding. The phone is extremely snappy, animations are as fluid as you could ask for, and my go-to mobile game (Call of Duty: Mobile) runs really well at High graphics and Max frame rate. For the way I use my phone, the Tensor G6 hasn’t given me any issues — and I’ve not noticed the Pixel 11 Pro heating up either. It’s been a really good experience.
bangla_paragraph5: That said, it has to be mentioned that the Tensor G6 still lacks significant raw horsepower versus the competition. Compared to the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 powering the Galaxy S26 and S26 Ultra, the Tensor G6 is worse in nearly every metric — delivering lower single-core and multi-core CPU speeds and significantly worse GPU performance (up to 58% slower in Wild Life Extreme 3DMark stress tests). The Tensor G6 delivers improved CPU performance compared to the Tensor G5 in the Pixel 10 Pro models, but I haven’t noticed any meaningful year-over-year difference.Joe Maring / Android AuthorityBenchmarks certainly aren’t everything, and as I said above, I’ve not had any real-world performance complaints with the Pixel 11 Pro after three weeks of regular use. I imagine most people who buy the 11 Pro or 11 Pro XL will find themselves in a similar boat. But if you want the absolute most performance from your next Android phone, you won’t find that here. That’s never been the point of Pixels, and I think that’s OK, but it’s still worth noting.One aspect of the Tensor G6 that’s unquestionably better is efficiency. The 4,850mAh battery in the Pixel 11 Pro and the 5,115mAh battery in Pixel 11 Pro XL are actually smaller than batteries in the Pixel 10 Pro and Pixel 10 Pro XL (4,870mAh and 5,200mAh, respectively), but this year’s phones still manage to last longer — and that’s all thanks to a more efficient chipset.Joe Maring / Android AuthorityI’ve primarily been using the small Pixel 11 Pro, and depending on what apps I’m using and how much of my time is spent on 5G, I’m seeing anywhere from four and a half to well over six hours of screen-on time, usually with around 20% battery still left in the tank. On the Pixel 10 Pro last year, I was topping out around five hours and hitting some days with just three hours of screen time.

title: Taiwan cracks down on tech businesses with illegal Chinese ownership — 166 investigations and at least 36 convictions since 2020
title_bn: তাইওয়ান অবৈধ চীনা মালিকানাধীন প্রযুক্তি ব্যবসায়ের বিরুদ্ধে কঠোর পদক্ষেপ নিয়েছে  ২০২০ সাল থেকে ১৬৬টি তদন্ত এবং কমপক্ষে ৩৬টি দোষী সাব্যস্ত হয়েছে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Taiwan's top investigative agency has been tracking Chinese businesses operating on the island without proper authority and shutting them down. These companies have been hiring Taiwanese experts to help with their semiconductor research and developme
paragraph1: Taiwan is cracking down on Chinese businesses illegally operating on the island, often by concealing their ownership through shell companies registered in other nations or by hiring non-Chinese nationals to put up the company for them. According to the Rest of World, Taiwan’s Cross-Strait Act and other related investment rules and regulations require Chinese businesses to apply for a permit from the government before they can began operating. However, not all can get this coveted approval, especially as political tensions between the island nation and its bigger neighbor has flared up in recent years.Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffsChina has been trying to build self-sufficiency when it comes to semiconductors and advanced chips — an endeavor that began in 2015 and was supercharged in recent years by the White House’s efforts to keep Western technologies away from Beijing through trade bans and export controls. Many Chinese companies are trying to stay competitive and build their own technologies by hiring experts and engineers from across the Taiwan Strait, especially those who have experience working in Taiwan’s vibrant semiconductor industry.
paragraph2: They’re even trying to attract talent by offering lucrative salaries that are five to ten times higher than average.However, Taipei considers this a threat to its national security, especially as its “silicon shield” strategy relies on its technological advantage over China to ensure that its allies help defend it in case of an invasion. Taiwan accounts for more than 60% of global semiconductor production and produces about 90% of the most advanced processors — so any disruption would plunge the modern world into chaos. And by building a semiconductor industry that can rival Taiwan's, China hopes to erode Taiwan’s advantage while also ensuring that it can have all the chips it needs without relying on external sources.The Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau (MJIB), the Taiwanese equivalent to the FBI, has investigated 166 cases involving illegal Chinese ownership since 2020.
paragraph3: Court records reveal that at least 36 of these have resulted in convictions, in which punishment can include prison time of up to three years and fines ranging from NTD 120,000 (USD $3,800) to nearly NTD 25,000,000 (USD $800,000).Of the 36 companies that been found guilty of violating the Cross-Strait Act, 33 of them were focused on semiconductor research, development, and design. Aside from this, the agency also investigated 67 cases of Chinese companies allegedly stealing trade secrets from Taiwanese companies.The Chinese companies accused of breaking Taiwan’s ownership law aren’t small entities, either. Some of the businesses that were investigated and raided were said to have connections with tech giant Xiaomi, smartphone brand OnePlus and mother company Oppo, and Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC), which is China’s most advanced foundry and a direct competitor to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation (TSMC).
paragraph4: Despite the fear that Beijing is using this technique for economic espionage, Omdia research director Hui He said that “These moves were largely driven by business needs.” Still, former U.S. Department of Defense official Nichol Eftimiades warned, “Is it espionage if I sit there poaching talents? Well, in some places it is.
paragraph5: We are dealing with different definitions depending on the country, and it’s a problem.”Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox. title: 4 reasons why I’ll always buy Samsung Galaxy phones over Pixels
title_bn: আমি কেন সবসময় স্যামসাং গ্যালাক্সি ফোন কিনবো তার চারটি কারণ
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Google has some catching up to do.
paragraph1: Robert Triggs / Android AuthorityAdd Android Authority on Google: I switch phones for a living, so I don’t say this lightly: Google makes great phones. But “great” and “the phone I’d actually buy and recommend to friends” are two very different things. I’ve used Galaxy and Pixel phones for years, and I always come back to a Galaxy.And no, this has nothing to do with foldables, the S Pen, or any of that stuff that only matters to a small group of users. It’s because of the experience that actually counts when you’re living with the same device for two or three years. Samsung just gets more of that right, at least for me. The Pixel 11 lineup hasn’t changed that.What matters most when picking a phone?36 votesI prefer Samsung’s apps over Google’sLet’s start with something that isn’t talked about enough in the whole Galaxy versus Pixel debate. Some of Samsung’s apps and features are way better, and that matters in day-to-day use.Samsung’s Secure Folder is a great example here. I know, I know, Pixel has Private Space too, but if you put them side by side, Secure Folder just does more. It’s more feature-rich, it doesn’t force you to use a secondary Google account, and you can hide it from the app drawer entirely. Samsung DeX is another underrated gem. I personally use it as a laptop replacement while traveling, and it gets the job done. Pixel’s Desktop Mode is barebones by comparison. Heck, it doesn’t even work wirelessly yet, which means you can’t use your phone freely for something else while the Desktop Mode is running.
paragraph2: These are just a couple of examples, but the pattern holds. Modes and Routines beats Pixel Rules thanks to a longer list of triggers and actions. Samsung Notes beats Google Keep with features like note summarization and easy PDF annotation. Samsung Gallery beats Google Photos because of its ease of use and a search tool that works for every photo, not just those backed up to the cloud. The list goes on.Of course, Google also makes great apps that are hard to beat — Photos, Drive, Calendar, Gboard, and Gemini. But here’s the thing. I can use every single one of those apps on my Galaxy if I want. That’s not true the other way around.One UI is more flexible and fun than Pixel UIAndy Walker / Android AuthorityOne of the big talking points for Pixel is the “clean” or “pure Android” experience — and sure, it is. But that only carries you so far. After a few weeks, that same minimalism starts feeling less like elegance and more like Google just didn’t bother.One UI is all about customization.I’m someone who fell in love with Android for its flexibility, and One UI delivers that. There are enough options that I can make my Galaxy look and behave exactly how I want. In fact, Good Lock is the single biggest reason I’d never switch to a Pixel. I know it can feel like a lot — overwhelming, even, if you’re new to it.
paragraph3: But that’s exactly why Samsung keeps it separate from One UI. Being able to redesign the keyboard, hide certain status bar icons, change the recent apps layout, set custom timeouts per app, create your own gestures, or build a DIY homescreen — these are the kinds of things that are hard to give up.I know not everyone cares about these things. Still, I’d rather have all these options and never touch them than not have them at all. It’s the same argument I made earlier with apps. I can absolutely set up a clean, minimalist experience on my Galaxy if I want. But on a Pixel, I can’t go the other direction.Galaxy phones still have the performance advantageRyan Whitwam / Android AuthorityEnough about software. I know a lot of Pixel fans genuinely don’t care about anything I just talked about, and that’s fair. So let’s talk about something that does affect literally everyone, which is performance. Most flagship Galaxy phones in the US ship with Snapdragon chips, and they outperform Google’s Tensor chips in raw power. Sure, Tensor has never been about chasing benchmark numbers, but that doesn’t mean Snapdragon chips don’t have a real edge here.If I’m paying flagship prices, I want a phone that works, and works reliably.Even if I ignore all of that noise, it still doesn’t change the fact that Pixels have some persistent issues that make them less reliable — and we’ve talked about those many times. Overheating is the biggest one, and there’s no hiding it. These aren’t one-off complaints either. They’ve followed nearly every Pixel in the last few years.
paragraph4: Then there are network-related issues, bugs like incoming calls not showing up, inconsistent battery life, and so on. These are all issues I’m just not ready to deal with on my primary device.Samsung phones obviously have their own problems, but not at this scale. If I’m paying flagship prices, I want a phone that works, and works reliably. Right now, that’s still a Galaxy.Samsung gives me more reasons to stay loyalZac Kew-Denniss / Android AuthorityThere’s one more thing that makes me want to buy a Galaxy, and that’s the ecosystem. I’m not exactly a fan of companies using it to lock us in, but I can’t ignore it either. When I buy a phone, I’m naturally more inclined to buy other products from that same brand. And this is another area where Samsung has a clear edge.Samsung’s Galaxy Books sync beautifully with Galaxy phones.The Galaxy Tab S lineup is the closest thing Android has to an iPad, while Google’s tablet situation is basically nonexistent at this point. The same goes for laptops. Say what you want about Windows laptops in general, but they are the only practical option for anyone who doesn’t want a Mac. Samsung’s Galaxy Books are a great pick here because they sync beautifully with Galaxy phones.For instance, I love how Phone Link lets me easily mirror and control my Galaxy phone from any PC while also syncing the clipboard between the two. I also like Samsung’s Multi Control feature, which lets me use the same keyboard and mouse from my Galaxy Book to control my Galaxy Tab or Galaxy phone. This even lets me drag and drop files between them.
paragraph5: My Galaxy Buds can also automatically switch between all my devices depending on what I’m doing, which is another benefit of a strong ecosystem. All of this might not matter to everyone, but it sure does to me since I spend most of my day in front of a screen.Beyond that, Samsung can also match Google’s ecosystem product for product, with Galaxy Buds, Galaxy Watch, and Galaxy Ring. There’s nothing missing.Pixel phones are better in some ways, but that’s not enoughZac Kew-Denniss / Android AuthorityLook, none of this means Pixel phones are bad or don’t have an edge over Galaxy phones in specific areas. They absolutely do. I’m a fan of Google’s camera processing, bloatware–free experience, faster updates, cleaner hardware designs, and all those Pixel-exclusive features. In a lot of ways, Pixel feels like an iPhone that just wants to keep things simple and focused.But for me, none of these advantages are big enough to outweigh everything else I’ve just talked about. So yes, even if Pixel wins on a few specific things, it’s not enough to change my mind. At least not yet.FollowThank you for being part of our community. Read our Comment Policy before posting.

title: Indian Listed New-Age Tech Company Tracker: Market Cap, Revenue & More
title_bn: ভারতীয় লিস্টেড নিউ-এজ টেক কোম্পানি ট্র্যাকার: মার্কেট ক্যাপ, রাজস্ব ও আরও
author: TechPulse
excerpt: For years, we at Inc42 have tracked the Indian tech startup ecosystem and seen it grow from a kid to…
paragraph1: SUMMARYOver 70 Indian new-age tech companies have already crossed the IPO milestone and are now listed on the bourses The cumulative market cap of listed new-age tech companies as of now exceeds $190 Bn 10 new-age companies — Turtlemint, Klassroom, Shiprocket, LEAP India, Kissht, Aye Finance, Fractal Analytics, Amagi, Shadowfax and SEDEMAC — have already made their public market debut in 2026 For years, we at Inc42 have tracked the Indian tech startup ecosystem and seen it grow from a kid to an adult. Among the clearest signs of evolution and maturity of this ecosystem is the growing number of startups eyeing a public listing now. For Indian companies, achieving a public listing has for long symbolised operational progression, transparency, and long-term viability. For startups, it’s a relatively new but increasingly critical rite of passage, one that not only signals coming of age but also creates pathways for investor exits and wealth creation.
paragraph2: Currently, nearly 15 startups, including Zepto, OYO, among others, are in various stages of their IPO journey. Meanwhile, over 60 Indian new-age tech companies have already crossed the milestone and are now listed on the bourses. The list now also includes Indian companies like MakeMyTrip and Freshworks, which are listed on Nasdaq in the US. India’s startup IPO wave reached its peak in 2025, surpassing the previous year’s momentum.
paragraph3: While 13 startups went public in 2024, the number has already been overtaken this year, with 18 companies making their market debut in the previous year. The list of new-age tech companies that went public in 2025 included Meesho, Ather Energy, Urban Company, Lenskart, Groww, Pine Labs and PhysicsWallah. The list is only expected to grow further this year. 10 new-age companies — Turtlemint, Klassroom, Shiprocket, LEAP India, Kissht, Aye Finance, Fractal Analytics, Amagi, Shadowfax and SEDEMAC — have already made their public market debut in 2026.
paragraph4: As of now, the total market capitalisation of the listed companies stands at over $173 Bn. To consolidate all the information about listed startups, Inc42 has launched the Indian Listed New-Age Tech Company Tracker. From the movement in the shares of the companies since their listing to the financial performance of these companies, the tracker is your one-stop resource to know everything you need about the listed tech companies. Among the clearest signs of evolution and maturity of this ecosystem is the growing number of startups eyeing a public listing now. For Indian companies, achieving a public listing has for long symbolised operational progression, transparency, and long-term viability. For startups, it’s a relatively new but increasingly critical rite of passage, one that not only signals coming of age but also creates pathways for investor exits and wealth creation.

India’s startup IPO wave reached its peak in 2025, surpassing the previous year’s momentum.

title: ESDS Listing Pushes New-Age Tech Stocks’ Market Cap Past $170 Bn
title_bn: ইএসডিএস তালিকাভুক্তকরণ নিউ-এজ টেক স্টককে  বাজার মূলধন  ১৭০ বিলিয়ন ডলার ছাড়িয়ে যেতে বাধ্য করেছে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The first week of September was marked by stake sales by institutional investors, fresh ESOP allotments, and continued momentum in…
paragraph1: The first week of September was marked by stake sales by institutional investors, fresh ESOP allotments, and continued momentum in the new-age tech IPO market. Of the 62 previously listed new-age tech stocks under Inc42’s coverage, 26 gained between 0.03% and 13% during the week, while the remaining 36 declined by up to 15%. Honasa ended the week flat. After leading the gainers last week, BSE SME-listed edtech startup Klassroom emerged as the biggest loser this week. Its shares fell 15.37% to end at ₹184.50. FirstCry also touched a fresh all-time low of ₹170 on Wednesday before recovering to close the week at ₹180.10. The stock fell 3.07% during the week and ended about 61% below its IPO price of ₹465. Shares of Ola Electric, Delhivery, Eternal, Swiggy, and Nykaa also ended the week marginally lower. Despite most stocks declining, the combined market capitalisation of the 62 previously listed new-age tech companies rose to $169.39 Bn from $166.91 Bn last week. Meanwhile, Lenskart, Ather Energy, and LEAP India touched fresh all-time highs during the week. NSE SME-listed Yudiz Solutions topped the gainers, rising ₹3.10, or 13%, during the week. Shiprocket, Urban Company, BlueStone, and Shadowfax also recorded sizable gains. ESDS Software Solution, which listed yesterday, became the 63rd listed new-age tech company. After its IPO was oversubscribed 135.9X, the enterprise cloud, data centre, GPU, and AI infrastructure company listed at a 74% premium on the BSE and 76.
paragraph2: 5% on the NSE over its issue price of ₹429. The stock subsequently hit the 20% upper circuit and ended its first trading session at ₹895.50 on the BSE and ₹908.40 on the NSE, more than doubling from its issue price. Including ESDS’ market capitalisation of about $1.11 Bn, the combined market cap of the 63 new-age tech companies crossed $170 Bn to reach approximately $170.50 Bn. Despite the sharp expansion in recent years, new-age tech companies account for just over 3% of the Indian stock market’s total capitalisation. With that, here’s a look at some of the other major developments of the week. Info Edge-Backed Meritto Files IPO Papers: After receiving SEBI’s clearance for its confidential DRHP, Meritto parent NoPaperForms filed its updated IPO papers. The proposed public issue comprises a fresh issue of shares worth ₹350 Cr and an OFS of up to 3.8 Cr equity shares. Info Edge will be the sole selling shareholder in the OFS. RentoMojo IPO Next Week: Furniture and appliance rental startup RentoMojo filed its RHP for its public issue, which will open for bidding on Wednesday and close on Friday. The company has set a price band of ₹384 to ₹404 per share. At the upper end, the ₹1,255.6 Cr IPO will comprise a ₹150 Cr fresh issue and an OFS of up to 2.7 Cr shares worth ₹1,105.6 Cr. Investors Pare Stakes: Institutional investors continued to pare their holdings in listed new-age tech companies through block deals. SoftBank offloaded shares worth ₹1,650 Cr in Meesho, while Alpha Wave sold Pine Labs shares worth ₹550 Cr. Lenskart and Eternal also saw shares worth ₹2,670.2 Cr and ₹3,265 Cr, respectively, change hands during the week.
paragraph3: Nykaa Raises Earth Rhythm Stake: Nykaa completed the acquisition of an additional 24.2% stake in skincare and personal care brand Earth Rhythm, increasing its ownership in the subsidiary to 18.6%. Purple Style Labs IPO Subscribed 1.29X: Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop parent Purple Style Labs’ ₹680 Cr IPO was subscribed 1.29X. Investors placed bids for 88.54 Lakh shares against the 68.49 Lakh shares on offer. The company’s shares are scheduled to debut on the stock exchanges on Monday. BlackRock Buys Ather Shares: Asset management giant BlackRock bought 25.9 Lakh shares of Ather Energy for ₹445.3 Cr through an open-market transaction. BlackRock Global Funds purchased the shares at ₹1,713.02 apiece as the electric two-wheeler maker’s stock continued to trade near its all-time high. Nazara Raises Funky Monkeys Stake: Nazara Technologies acquired an additional 4.1% stake in Funky Monkeys Play Centre for ₹1.90 Cr through a secondary transaction with founder Binita Putcha. The acquisition of 75,972 shares increased Nazara’s holding in the indoor play-centre chain to 68.1% from 64%. Fractal Liquidates Sweden Arm: Fractal Analytics initiated the voluntary liquidation of its step-down subsidiary Fractal Analytics Sweden AB. The AI company said the move was aimed at simplifying its corporate structure and reducing administrative and legal compliance costs. RECOMMENDED FOR yOU Now, let’s take a look at the performance of the broader market this week.
paragraph4: Global Rate Risks Weigh On Markets Indian equity markets extended their decline for the fourth consecutive week. The Nifty 50 fell 1.15% during the week to close at 23,897.70, while the Sensex declined nearly 1% to 76,515.43. Rising crude oil prices, geopolitical tensions, and uncertainty around global interest rates weighed on investor sentiment. A marginal recovery yesterday snapped a four-session losing streak, but the rebound remained limited amid concerns over foreign investor flows and elevated global bond yields. Brent crude emerged as a key pressure point, rising about 7% during the week to hover around $96 per barrel as escalating US-Iran tensions raised concerns over energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz. Higher crude prices could add to India’s inflation and current-account pressures and weigh on the margins of companies sensitive to energy and other input costs. Global interest-rate expectations also remained a major driver. US non-farm payrolls rose by a stronger-than-expected 1.62 Lakh in August, increasing expectations of a potential rate hike by the US Federal Reserve. Dovish comments from Fed governor Christopher Waller, however, offered some relief earlier in the week. Domestic indicators offered some support, with India’s GDP growing 7.8% YoY in Q1 FY27 and gross GST collections rising 14.8% YoY to ₹1.99 Lakh Cr in August. Ajit Mishra, SVP of research at Religare Broking, expects markets to remain sensitive to crude prices, geopolitical developments, and global monetary policy. He sees 23,600-23,700 as the Nifty’s immediate support zone, with resistance at 24,150-24,200. Geojit Investments chief investment strategist VK Vijayakumar said FPI flows had turned positive, with foreign investors pumping ₹2,374 Cr into Indian equities during the first four days of September. However, he cautioned that rising global bond yields could limit sustained inflows. Against this backdrop, let’s take a closer look at the performance of LEAP India and Ola Electric. LEAP India Slips Despite Profit Growth LEAP India’s shares came under pressure despite the recently listed logistics company reporting healthy YoY growth in its first quarterly results since going public.
paragraph5: The stock fell 10.65% during the week to close at ₹150.55, taking its market capitalisation to about ₹6,632.3 Cr, (about $700 Mn). LEAP India’s consolidated net profit rose 30.3% YoY to ₹24.7 Cr in Q1 FY27, while operating revenue increased 19.1% to ₹203.4 Cr. EBITDA grew 21% to ₹114.1 Cr, with the margin expanding 108 basis points to 53.5%. However, sequential growth remained muted. Revenue was largely unchanged from ₹203.5 Cr in Q4 FY26, while net profit declined 5.6% QoQ. LEAP India listed on August 14 at a premium of 4.4% to its ₹159 issue price. However, the stock has since fallen below the issue price, with investors likely to focus on whether the company can sustain its targeted revenue growth of more than 20%, improve asset utilisation, and translate its expansion into higher earnings. The company has identified higher asset movement, cross-selling, expansion into new industries, and growth in its GCC operations as its key growth drivers. Meanwhile, broad analyst coverage of the stock is yet to emerge. Ola Electric Ends Lower Ola Electric’s shares fell 1.92% during the week to ₹38.

title: Google Photos on Android just got an iPhone feature I’ve waited a year for — how to use it now
title_bn: অ্যান্ড্রয়েডে গুগল ফটোতে আইফোনের একটি বৈশিষ্ট্য এসেছে আমি এক বছর ধরে অপেক্ষা করেছি  এখন কিভাবে এটি ব্যবহার করবেন
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Manual! Photo! Stacks! Are! Here!
paragraph1: Joe Maring / Android AuthorityAdd Android Authority on Google: In May 2025, the Google Photos app got an incredible feature: the ability to manually create photo stacks. Google Photos has long automatically created stacks of similar-looking pictures, helping to better organize your library. However, that automated process doesn’t always work as you’d like, leaving your Photos library more chaotic than you’d prefer.Manual stacking fixes that issue perfectly — but there’s been just one problem: it’s been exclusive to the Photos app on iOS. There’s been evidence of manual stacking coming to the Android app for a while, but month after month, it’s remained MIA.However, after over a year of not-so-patiently waiting, that’s finally changed — and I couldn’t be happier.What do you need to access manual photo stacks on Google Photos?
paragraph2: Taylor Kerns / Android AuthorityAs is always the case with Google app updates, an important question arises: What do you need to access this new feature?I first noticed the option for manual photo stacking in the Photos app on my Pixel 11 Pro running version 7.90.0.973970263. Manual stacking also appeared on my Pixel 11 Pro XL, with its Photos app on version 7.91.
paragraph3: 0.973540846.Interestingly, manual stacking is not currently available on my Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra running the Photos app on version 7.90.0.971743778. As is often the case with Google, it’s likely that manual stacking is part of a server-side rollout.
paragraph4: Be sure to check the Play Store for any updates to Google Photos, but if none are available and you still don’t see manual stacking on your app, you may just need to play the waiting game.How to create manual stacks in the Photos Android appJoe Maring / Android AuthorityCreating photo stacks in the Google Photos Android app follows the exact same steps as in the iOS app, which is to say, it’s extremely easy. To create a manual photo stack: Press and hold on the pictures you want to stack. Swipe left on the pop-up bar at the bottom of the screen. Tap Stack photos. As soon as you do this, those selected photos are grouped into a single stack in your Photos library. For example, if you selected five standalone images from your camera roll, they are now grouped into a single icon in your main library.
paragraph5: When you open the stack, you can scroll through all of the stacked photos from there.The actual process of manually creating photo stacks is extremely simple, but with no official announcement from Google that the feature is finally available in the Android app, it’s very easy to overlook.Automatic stacking will still happen like it always has, but you now have the option to manually organize things, too. It may sound like a small feature, but as someone who’s been creating manual stacks in the iOS app since last year, it’s genuinely one of my favorite organization tools in Google Photos.FollowThank you for being part of our community. bangla_paragraph4: Google ফটোতে কোনও আপডেট জন্য প্লে স্টোরটি পরীক্ষা করে দেখুন, তবে যদি কোনওটিই উপলভ্য না থাকে এবং আপনি এখনও আপনার অ্যাপ্লিকেশনটিতে ম্যানুয়াল স্ট্যাকিং না দেখেন তবে আপনার কেবল অপেক্ষা করার খেলা খেলতে হবে। ফটো অ্যান্ড্রয়েড অ্যাপে ম্যান্যুয়াল স্টাকগুলি কীভাবে তৈরি করবেনJoe Maring / Android AuthorityGoogle ফটো অ্যানড্রয়েডে অ্যাপে ফটো স্ট্যাক তৈরি করা আইওএস অ্যাপের মতোই একই পদক্ষেপ অনুসরণ করে, যা বলা হয়, এটি অত্যন্ত সহজ। একটি ম্যানুটিয়াল ফটো স্টাক তৈরি করতেঃ আপনি যে ছবিগুলি স্ট্যাক করতে চান তা টিপুন এবং ধরে রাখুন। সোয়াইপ করুন
bangla_paragraph5: আপনি যখন স্ট্যাকটি খুলবেন, তখন আপনি সেখান থেকে সমস্ত স্ট্যাকযুক্ত ফটো দিয়ে স্ক্রোল করতে পারবেন। ম্যানুয়ালি ফটো স্ট্যাক তৈরির প্রকৃত প্রক্রিয়াটি অত্যন্ত সহজ, তবে গুগল থেকে কোনও আনুষ্ঠানিক ঘোষণা না থাকায় যে বৈশিষ্ট্যটি অবশেষে অ্যান্ড্রয়েড অ্যাপে উপলব্ধ, এটি উপেক্ষা করা খুব সহজ। স্বয়ংক্রিয় স্ট্যাকিং এখনও আগের মতোই ঘটবে, তবে আপনার কাছে এখন ম্যানুটিয়ালি জিনিসগুলি সংগঠিত করার বিকল্প রয়েছে। এটি একটি ছোট বৈশিষ্ট্য বলে মনে হতে পারে, তবে কেউ যারা ম্যান্যুয়াল স্ট্যাকগুলি তৈরি করছে

title: 5 Android apps you should use instead of Google Keep
title_bn: গুগল কেপের পরিবর্তে আপনার যে ৫টি অ্যান্ড্রয়েড অ্যাপ ব্যবহার করা উচিত
author: TechPulse
excerpt: There are better ways to keep notes than Keep.
paragraph1: Megan Ellis / Android AuthorityAdd Android Authority on Google: Google Keep is a popular note-taking app, especially among those looking for a simple app for quick note-taking. It’s free, lightweight, and easy to use. Plus, it automatically syncs your notes across all devices at no extra cost and without additional configuration.Having said that, Google Keep has its own share of limitations. No rich-text editor, lack of proper note-organization options, and missing end-to-end encryption are a few common reasons people ditch Keep. If you’re in the same boat, here are some popular Google Keep alternatives you can check out.Which of these Google Keep alternatives would you switch to?39 votesNotallyXYash Wate / Android AuthorityNotallyX is an Android-only note-taking app that closely mimics Google Keep, which makes it ideal for quick note-taking. You can even create checklists, and the app supports attachments, just like Keep. It displays notes as cards, and you can color-code notes for quick visual identification.Unlike Keep, though, NotallyX is a local-first notes app, meaning it doesn’t sync your notes to a native cloud-based service by default; your notes stay on your device locally. This is nice for those who want complete control over their notes.
paragraph2: You can use Syncthing-Fork to set up cloud syncing and sync notes to other Android devices. NotallyX also supports rich-text formatting to help you format your notes better. It even lets you auto-delete items in your trash and configure auto-backup frequency, among other things. SimplenoteYash Wate / Android AuthoritySimplenote is another great Google Keep alternative. While it doesn’t closely mimic the Keep experience like NotallyX, it’s your best option if you’re like me and use a multi-ecosystem device setup, as it has apps for all major platforms and keeps notes synced. The app is completely free, and just like Keep, it’s ideal for jotting down quick notes. Notes appear in a list, and you can use tags (similar to labels in Keep) to keep them organized. Support for rich media is missing, and your notes aren’t end-to-end encrypted.As for the differences, Simplenote natively supports Markdown, which is excellent for quick note styling — though you miss out on whatever limited text-editing options you get with Keep. Then there’s the ability to access a note’s version history for times when you need it. You can also collaborate on a note with other Simplenote users and publish your notes to the web for anyone with the link to access them. Standard NotesMitja Rutnik / Android AuthorityStandard Notes is a cross-platform notes app that employs zero-knowledge end-to-end encryption.
paragraph3: This means your notes remain encrypted at all times, whether they’re on your phone, on the app’s servers, or in transit. And that’s the biggest reason you’d want to consider it over other apps. Unlike Keep, though, Standard Notes’ interface is quite different — it’s closer to Simplenote’s. That said, it’s quite customizable and packs plenty of options to play around with.Creating and jotting notes in Standard Notes is straightforward, and there’s support for tags to make organizing and finding similar notes easy. Notes are automatically synced to the app’s servers and available on your other devices. However, coming from Keep, you’ll miss the text-editing options Google’s notes app offered, since the Standard Notes text editor is bare-bones on the free plan.You can upgrade to a paid plan to get editing options and Markdown support. This will also unlock the ability to add attachments, use an advanced note editor, enable automated cloud backups, access extended version history, and more. NotesnookMegan Ellis / Android AuthorityNotesnook is one of the best free note-taking apps I’ve tried, packing features you won’t find in most free apps. And best of all, it provides zero-knowledge end-to-end encryption, so only you can access your notes. The Notesnook app differs from Keep and the alternatives we’ve discussed so far in several respects, be it its interface, note-taking experience, or customizability.
paragraph4: But if you find Keep too limiting and want an app that syncs notes for free without compromising on privacy, it fits the bill just right. I ditched Simplenote for Notesnook a while ago and have been using it to capture fleeting thoughts and ideas across all my devices.With Notesnook, you get a rich-text editor that lets you structure notes exactly how you want. The editor is highly customizable, too, which is a rare sight. There’s also support for media attachments, as well as the ability to embed items and create tables. As for organizing notes, you can group similar notes using tags. Or you may create notebooks (folders) to keep similar notes in one place. Among other things, the Notesnook app offers a slew of customization options, so you can change its appearance and behavior as needed. JoplinYash Wate / Android AuthorityJoplin is a popular note-taking app for creating structured notes. If you want to replace Keep with an app that’s suitable for long-form writing, research, or setting up a personal knowledge base, Joplin is your best bet. It’s free to use, open-source, and secures your notes using end-to-end encryption. Most importantly, it’s local-first, meaning your notes stay on your device until you decide to sync them.
paragraph5: And when you wish to do that, you can either store them on Joplin Cloud, which requires a paid subscription, or keep them on your preferred cloud storage service or personal cloud.Talking about features, Joplin has a rich-text editor similar to Notesnook, so you can customize it per your needs. Plus, there’s support for Markdown if you prefer it. Joplin also lets you add attachments, and you can even convert your notes into to-dos. Similarly, it has a built-in document scanner for turning physical documents into Joplin notes.When it comes to organizing notes, you can use tags and notebooks (sub-notebooks). What truly stands out about the app, though, is its support for plugins, which allow you to customize its appearance and do things it can’t do natively. All of the above Keep alternatives are either completely free to use or offer a generous free tier. So try them out for yourself to find out which one best serves your note-taking needs. title: This Android smartphone has a detachable GoPro-like camera, and we tried it!
title_bn: এই অ্যান্ড্রয়েড স্মার্টফোনটিতে একটি অপসারণযোগ্য গোপ্রো-এর মতো ক্যামেরা রয়েছে, এবং আমরা এটি চেষ্টা করেছি!
author: TechPulse
excerpt: A rugged Android phone with a camera you can pop off and use on its own? Yep, someone actually built one.
paragraph1: Add Android Authority on Google: Most smartphone makers are busy making their built-in cameras better every year, but at IFA 2026, I came across a phone taking a very different approach. Ulefone sub-brand, RugOne, has packed a GoPro-like action camera into the Xsnap 7 Pro, and the best part is, you can literally pop it right out of the phone.Where the action isAdamya Sharma / Android AuthorityThe detachable camera uses a magnetic connection to attach to the back of the Xsnap 7 Pro, with an additional physical safety lock to ensure it doesn’t accidentally fall out. That’s useful for a phone designed for outdoor enthusiasts, but it also makes removing the camera a little fiddly.Getting enough leverage to release the camera was almost impossible for me.I have long fingernails, and getting enough leverage to release the camera was almost impossible for me. Once it’s out, though, the idea gets much more interesting.
paragraph2: The camera can record at up to 2.8K at 30fps, while dropping to 1440p lets you record at up to 50fps. It can capture both vertical and horizontal video, and it has 64GB of built-in storage. The camera itself can record for up to 40 minutes on a single full charge and is waterproof to a depth of 5 meters.It connects to the phone via Wi-Fi 6 and can operate up to 50 meters away from the handset. The camera also charges while it’s docked inside the phone, and RugOne says it can fully recharge in around 35 minutes.The clever part is the Xsnap Pro appAdamya Sharma / Android AuthorityThe real trick isn’t just being able to pull the camera off the phone.
paragraph3: RugOne has built a dedicated XSnap Pro app that lets you see what the camera is recording and access the footage on the phone.That opens up some genuinely cool possibilities. For example, if you’re out with another person, one person can carry the detachable camera while the other holds the phone and watches the live view from almost 50 meters away. You can also start recording using a button on the camera itself or trigger it from the phone.You don't have to treat the detachable camera like a completely separate device.Once you’re done, the footage is accessible from the phone, so you don’t have to treat the detachable camera like a completely separate device.It’s a neat trick, particularly for outdoor activities where you might want to place the camera somewhere that isn’t very convenient for a phone, or simply have someone else operate it while you monitor what’s being captured.
paragraph4: The phone itself is no slouchAdamya Sharma / Android AuthorityThe Xsnap 7 Pro is a rugged Android phone aimed squarely at outdoor enthusiasts. It’s powered by MediaTek’s Dimensity 8400 chipset and comes with 12GB of RAM and 512GB of storage, with expandable storage available. There’s also eSIM support.I'm not sure the phone is a replacement for a dedicated action camera.Elsewhere, the device features a 6.67-inch display with a 120Hz refresh rate, while the rear camera setup includes a 50MP primary camera with OIS and a 64MP infrared night-vision camera paired with dedicated IR LEDs. And because this is a rugged phone, it gets an IP69K rating for dust and water resistance.
paragraph5: I’m not sure the phone is a replacement for a dedicated action camera based on my brief hands-on time, but I can see the appeal. The ability to physically separate the camera from the phone, watch its live feed remotely, trigger it from either device, and have the footage land back on the phone makes this much more interesting than simply sticking another camera on the back of a smartphone.The RugOne XSnap 7 Pro will debut at IFA this weekend before heading to Kickstarter on September 7, where it will be discounted for early-bird backers. It’s expected to launch globally next month for €1,099 (~$1,276).FollowThank you for being part of our community. Read our Comment Policy before posting.
bangla_paragraph1: গুগলে অ্যান্ড্রয়েড কর্তৃপক্ষ যুক্ত করুন: বেশিরভাগ স্মার্টফোন নির্মাতারা প্রতি বছর তাদের অন্তর্নির্মিত ক্যামেরা আরও ভাল করতে ব্যস্ত, তবে আইএফএ ২০২৬-এ আমি একটি ফোনের সাথে দেখা করেছি যা খুব আলাদা পদ্ধতি গ্রহণ করে। ইউলেফোনের উপ-ব্র্যান্ড, রগওন, এক্সন্যাপ 7 প্রো-তে একটি গোপ্রো-এর মতো অ্যাকশন ক্যামেরা প্যাক করেছে এবং সর্বোত্তম অংশটি হ'ল আপনি এটি ফোন থেকে সরাসরি পপ করতে পারেন। যেখানে অ্যাকশনের কাজটি হচ্ছেআদম্য শর্মা / অ্যান্ড্ৰয়েড অথরিটি।
bangla_paragraph2: ক্যামেরাটি 30fps এ 2.8K পর্যন্ত রেকর্ড করতে পারে, যখন 1440p এ হ্রাস করা আপনাকে 50fps পর্যন্ত রেকর্ডে অনুমতি দেয়। এটি উল্লম্ব এবং অনুভূমিক উভয় ভিডিও ক্যাপচার করতে পারে এবং এটিতে 64GB অন্তর্নির্মিত স্টোরেজ রয়েছে। ক্যামেরা নিজেই একক পূর্ণ চার্জে 40 মিনিটের জন্য রেকর্ডিং করতে পারে। এবং 5 মিটার গভীরতার জলরোধী। এটি ওয়াই-ফাই 6 এর মাধ্যমে ফোনে সংযুক্ত হয় এবং হ্যান্ডসেট থেকে 50 মিটার পর্যন্ত কাজ করতে পারে । ক্যামেরা এছাড়াও ফোনের ভিতরে ডক করার সময় চার্জ করে এবং রগওন বলে যে এটি আয়ারে সম্পূর্ণরূপে রিচার্জ করতে পারে
bangla_paragraph3: RugOne একটি ডেডিকেটেড XSnap Pro অ্যাপ তৈরি করেছে যা আপনাকে ক্যামেরা কী রেকর্ড করছে তা দেখতে এবং ফোনে ফুটেজ অ্যাক্সেস করতে দেয়। এটি কিছু সত্যিকারের দুর্দান্ত সম্ভাবনা উন্মুক্ত করে। উদাহরণস্বরূপ, আপনি যদি অন্য ব্যক্তির সাথে বাইরে থাকেন তবে একজন ব্যক্তি অপসারণযোগ্য ক্যামেরা বহন করতে পারেন যখন অন্য ব্যক্তি ফোনটি ধরে রাখে এবং প্রায় 50 মিটার দূরে থেকে লাইভ ভিউ দেখেন। আপনি ক্যামেরার নিজের একটি বোতাম ব্যবহার করে রেকর্ডিং শুরু করতে পারেন বা এটি ফোন থেকে ট্রিগার করতে পারেন। আপনাকে অপসরণযোগ্য ক্যামেরাকে একটি সি হিসাবে আচরণ করতে হবে না
bangla_paragraph4: ফোনটি নিজেই কোনও স্ল্যাশ নয়অ্যাডামিয়া শর্মা / অ্যান্ড্রয়েড কর্তৃপক্ষএক্সস্ন্যাপ 7 প্রো হ'ল একটি শক্ত অ্যান্ড্রেড ফোন যা সরাসরি বহিরঙ্গন উত্সাহীদের লক্ষ্য করে। এটি মিডিয়াটেকের ডাইমেনসিটি 8400 চিপসেট দ্বারা চালিত এবং 12 গিগাবাইট র্যাম এবং 512 গিগাবিট স্টোরেজ সহ উপলব্ধ স্টোমেজ সহ আসে। এছাড়াও ইএসআইএম সমর্থন রয়েছে। আমি নিশ্চিত নই যে ফোনটি একটি ডেডিকেটেড অ্যাকশন ক্যামেরার প্রতিস্থাপন। অন্যথায়, ডিভাইসে একটি 6.67 ইঞ্চি ডিসপ্লে রয়েছে 120Hz রিফ্রেশ রেট সহ, যখন পিছনের ক্যামেরা সেটআপটিতে 50MP প্রাইমা অন্তর্ভুক্ত রয়েছে।
bangla_paragraph5: আমি নিশ্চিত নই যে ফোনটি আমার সংক্ষিপ্ত হ্যান্ডস-অন সময়ের উপর ভিত্তি করে একটি ডেডিকেটেড অ্যাকশন ক্যামেরার প্রতিস্থাপন, তবে আমি আবেদনটি দেখতে পাচ্ছি। ক্যামেরাটি ফোন থেকে শারীরিকভাবে আলাদা করার ক্ষমতা, দূরবর্তীভাবে এর লাইভ ফিডটি দেখুন, এটি উভয় ডিভাইস থেকে ট্রিগার করুন এবং ফুটেজটি ফোনটিতে ফিরে আসুন এটি একটি স্মার্টফোনের পিছনে অন্য ক্যামেরা আটকে দেওয়ার চেয়ে অনেক বেশি আকর্ষণীয় করে তোলে। রগওয়ান এক্সএসএনএপ 7 প্রো 7 সেপ্টেম্বর কিকস্টার্টার যাওয়ার আগে এই সপ্তাহান্তে আইএফএতে আত্মপ্রকাশ করবে, যেখানে আমি

Healthtech and cleantech accounted for most of the week’s funding, raising a combined $120.8 Mn across nine deals. Together, they captured nearly 68% of the total raised by Indian startups during the week. paragraph3: Ultrahuman’s $70 Mn round made up 94% of the sector’s total funding. Cleantech trailed healthtech with five startups raising $46.3 Mn this week. Yuma Energy’s $35 Mn fundraise provided the biggest boost, accounting for a substantial chunk of the sector’s haul. Beyond the top two sectors, advanced hardware and technology and ecommerce segments saw four funding deals materialise apiece. Early-stage funding remained active, with six startups collectively raising around $12 Mn across seed, pre-seed and pre-Series A rounds. The week also saw three startups raise undisclosed amounts in equity. On the investor front, Equentis and Info Edge Ventures were the week’s most active backers, participating in two startup deals each. Startup M&As This Week upGrad completed the acquisition of Unacademy for just over $200 Mn, marking a more than 90% drop from its $3.5 Bn peak valuation in 2021. Adobe acquired Peak XV Partners’ backed startup Rilo, backed by Peak XV Partners, for an undisclosed amount. It is Adobe’s second Indian startup acquisition after Rephrase.

Startup IPO Developments This Week After an overwhelming investor response to its IPO, AI cloud provider ESDS Software Solution made a strong public market debut, listing at an over 75% premium on the bourses. The stock closed at ₹908.4, gaining 111.7% on its first trading day. After ESDS, Yotta Data Services is also planning to go public. The company is likely to file its draft papers with SEBI by October, eyeing the raise of up to $1.5 Bn via its IPO.

The round could see participation from Neo Group, Kado Global and Moore Strategic Ventures.
